contribution.position: I hold my earlier position. I am answering qa's claim on axis:risk that run_time is 45s, comfortably inside the 60s budget. That figure does not appear in artifact:perf-report, which records 118s at peak load against the 60s budget. If a 45s measurement exists, it is missing from the artifact list, and it would have to be a non-peak run. Peak is the condition under which retry storms occurred, so 45s cannot offset the 118s result. I also checked ops's claim that operations can run this. artifact:ops-runbook, as described, covers deploy and rollback steps only. Nothing in it addresses retry or timeout settings, and a rollback does not stop a retry storm already in progress. Product's cost margin (+3% against a 5% ceiling) is not about reliability. artifact:incident-log shows two sev2 incidents last quarter, both retry storms, so the 118s overshoot is the open item. What would settle it: retry and timeout settings checked against 118s, a peak-load test showing bounded retries, or a documented waiver or revised budget for the 60s target. I would update if the 45s source is produced and shown to be a peak-load run, or if the bounded-retry evidence arrives.
